newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to reduce minimum state stake in Matav, OTP.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to reduce minimum state stake in Matav, OTP.

text.p: The Hungarian government plans to amend the privatisation bill's regulations on what stakes the state should maintain permanently in some companies, government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.

"The change affects 80 companies, reducing the state stake in most...increasing it in others...and there are also new companies on the list," Kiss told a news conference following the government meeting.

Government plans include the reduction of the compulsory state stake to one golden share from the present mandatory 25 percent plus one share in Matav Rt and the same reduction for Orszagos Takarekpenztar es Kereskedelmi Bank Rt.
The government plans to raise the minimum state holding to 50 percent plus one share from 25 percent plus one share for state broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Rt.
New entries to the list include Pick Szeged Rt, in which the minimum state stake should be one golden share and FEG Army Fegyvergayrto Kft, with a minimal state stake of 50 percent plus one share.
Kiss added that the planned changes would also transfer the state's voting rights to the relevant ministries from privatisation agency APV Rt.
